bullets.title: July CPI In-Line Reduces September Rate-Hike Odds to ~36-45%
bullets.body: July headline CPI came in at +3.4% YoY (+0.1% MoM) and core at +2.5% YoY (+0.2% MoM), all four readings matching consensus. September Fed hike odds fell ~11-12pp to 36-45% depending on market. Goldman Sachs and Baird called the data 'encouraging' and argue the Fed will hold in September; Santander is an outlier still expecting a September hike on unrounded core at 2.6% annualized. Core goods prices rose 0.20% MoM, largest since Sept 2025, and energy price relief may be temporary as crude and refining margins rise.

bullets.title: JPM Tactically Bullish Into Jackson Hole; Expects Market to Run Higher
bullets.body: JPMorgan remains Tactically Bullish, favoring a Tech/Cyclicals barbell, and expects markets to rally into Jackson Hole (Aug 26-29). Positioning is supportive as de-grossing/de-leveraging is complete; dealers are short gamma into mid-September. The firm suggests delaying full deployment until after upcoming CPI and Retail Sales prints.

bullets.title: Yardeni Raises S&P 500 Target to 8,400 on 'Fabulous Earnings Momentum'
bullets.body: Ed Yardeni raised his S&P 500 year-end target to 8,400 from 8,250, boosting his 2026 S&P EPS forecast to $375 from $330, citing broad earnings beats and strong corporate momentum. The Fear & Greed Index moved into greed territory at 62/100.

bullets.title: 10-Year Treasury Auction Tails at Highest Yield Since 2007 (4.683%)
bullets.body: The $46B 10-year note auction priced at 4.683%, up 10bps from the prior auction at 4.580% — the highest yield since 2007. The bid-cover declined to 2.53 from 2.59, and foreign (indirect) bidders fell to 76.7% from 81.5%, offset by domestics at 14.7% vs 10.7%. JPM maintains 2s/10s steepeners and expects tomorrow's $25B 30-year auction to require concession. One observer called it a 'regime change' in fixed income.

bullets.title: U.S. Federal Budget Deficit Widens to $432B — $86B Wider Than Forecast
bullets.body: The U.S. federal budget deficit came in at $432.308 billion, much wider than the $346 billion forecast and well above the prior month's $120 billion. This adds to fiscal concerns underpinning the backup in long-end Treasury yields.

bullets.title: Yield Curve Steepening Favors Regional Banks and Cyclicals; 22V Bullish on Hyperscalers
bullets.body: 22V Research expects the yield curve to steepen over time, creating a favorable backdrop for regional banks and cyclicals. Separately, Mag7/hyperscalers trade more than 2 standard deviations below their 2018-Q3 mean, implying ~30% upside to one std dev below mean. AI CapEx slowdown risk could be offset by productivity-driven consumer surplus, Fed easing, and housing recovery.

bullets.title: Goldman Forecasts Core PCE at 0.23% for July — Slightly Above Consensus
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs expects July core PCE to rise 0.23% MoM, modestly above core CPI and consensus, with portfolio management fees adding ~8bps from Q2 equity gains. The firm also flagged potential volatility from upcoming BEA methodology changes.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Demand Remains Capacity-Constrained, Not Demand-Constrained
bullets.body: Multiple earnings calls (NBIS, CRWV, SMCI, LITE) confirm AI infrastructure backlogs grew ~150% YoY to ~$1.7T vs. capex growth of ~80%. NBIS Q2 revenue surged 454% YoY to $582M with 40.6% adj. EBITDA margin; CRWV backlog surged 250% to $104B+. Net new ARR also up ~150% across tracked neoclouds. The read-through is that deployable, production-ready capacity — not end demand — is the constraint.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Near-Standstill: Only 14 Vessels vs. 120/Day Pre-War
bullets.body: Iran reaffirmed the Strait of Hormuz closure with no policy change despite Trump's claim of U.S. 'total control.' Kpler data shows only 14 vessels crossed the Strait on Tuesday vs. a pre-war average of ~120/day. US intelligence now expects Iran-related oil supply disruptions to persist through end of 2027, and US-Iran diplomatic talks remain stalled.

bullets.title: Crude Inventories Surge 17.4M Barrels — Largest Jump Since January 2023
bullets.body: U.S. crude oil inventories jumped 17.423 million barrels against an expected draw of 1.8 million barrels, the largest weekly build since January 2023. Cushing rose 1.6M barrels. Gasoline and distillates were modestly negative. Saudi Arabia resumed loadings at its Ras Tanura complex after a month-long absence, suggesting partial supply recovery from the Persian Gulf.

bullets.title: OPEC Cuts Oil-Demand Forecast Again as Energy Threatens to Reignite Inflation
bullets.body: OPEC lowered its global oil-demand outlook for another month. Separately, falling energy prices helped cool July CPI (gasoline -2.9% MoM, fuel oil -1.7%), but rising crude prices and strong refining margins are already pushing fuel costs higher, threatening an August re-acceleration in energy-driven inflation.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Debt Market: Hyperscalers Have ~$2T of Incremental Debt Capacity
bullets.body: Per a Goldman Sachs debt capital markets podcast, AI infrastructure debt issuance is 'staggering' and crowding out other IG market supply. Hyperscalers collectively hold ~$2T of incremental debt capacity while maintaining IG ratings. The AI credit universe stratifies into 4 risk layers; primary risk in Layer 1 (hyperscaler senior unsecured) is technical spread widening. Separately, CME is launching compute futures contracts effective October 5.

bullets.title: Data Center REIT Sector Outperforms on $2.25T AI-Factory Commitment Wave
bullets.body: S&P 500 Data Center REITs rose 3.44% on the day (YTD +34.57%) as NVDA, BAC, and Morgan Stanley announced combined $2.25T AI-factory investment commitments. FRMI surged 7% on a 2.6GW power strategic alliance. ERCOT lowered its FY27 power demand forecast to +5.6% (down 8.4ppts) due to a data center moratorium; Wood Mackenzie estimates only ~28% of requested data center capacity will materialize.

bullets.title: Norway's $2.3T Sovereign Wealth Fund Posts Record H1 Profit but CEO Warns Gains Won't Last
bullets.body: Norway's sovereign wealth fund delivered a 12.95% return in H1, posting a record $185 billion profit driven by surging semiconductor stocks. CEO Nicolai Tangen warned that investors should not expect similar returns ahead — a notable macro sentiment signal from the world's largest sovereign fund.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS Yield Hits 99% but ABF Substrate and Memory Remain AI Chip Bottlenecks
bullets.body: TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging yield cleared 99%, removing one supply constraint for AI chips. However, ABF (substrate) and DRAM remain binding bottlenecks. ABF requires $100M-$500M investment plus 18-24 months for specialized tooling; DRAM fabs require $15-20B+ and 3+ years. Substrates are expected to clear before DRAM. CXMT meanwhile reports 90% DDR5 yield, adding Chinese supply pressure to the memory market.

bullets.title: Open-Weight AI Models Shift Value to Compute/Inference; Morgan Stanley Favors AMZN and GOOGL
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues open-weight models (including Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 and Google Gemini Flash) create downward pricing pressure on model labs but benefit hyperscalers through compute scarcity and volume. Hyperscalers are expected to generate 20-60% ROIC on owned GB300 hardware even at lower token pricing (~$1.75/M tokens). MS maintains Overweight on AMZN and GOOGL on lowest-cost-to-serve positioning via custom silicon. NBIS confirmed AI cloud market is capacity- not demand-constrained.

bullets.title: Capex Deceleration Thesis Emerges: Growth Rate Slowing as Capacity Catches Up to Demand
bullets.body: Multiple sources note AI capex remains high in absolute terms but growth rate is decelerating as capacity catches up with demand. Hyperscaler FCF is improving and new-issue supply expectations are declining, causing credit spreads to tighten. Separately, a credit market headline flagged 'rising doubts over AI buildout' sustainability.

bullets.title: VIX at 7-Month Low of 14.84; SPY Call Walls at 775-780 Signal Continued Bullish Positioning
bullets.body: The CBOE Volatility Index briefly hit a 7-month low at 14.84. SPY shows $4.4B in call open interest at the 775 strike and $4.3B at 780, with bulls maintaining control per options positioning. Unusual large call buying ($1.4M) also observed in META at the 800 strike (37% OTM), and a whale doubled down on NVDA calls 2 days ago for a $1.5M profit.

bullets.title: Red Sea and Black Sea Shipping Severely Disrupted; Ukraine Suspends Tanker Attacks
bullets.body: Red Sea shipping fell from ~120 ships/day pre-war to as few as 2/day; Saudi crude loadings are now completed with tracking disabled. Odesa port traffic is down ~60% YoY to 159 vessels in July from ~400, due to Russian drone attacks. Ukraine suspended attacks on Black Sea tankers at Vance's urging. Black Sea oil tanker rates hit record highs amid the disruption.

bullets.title: Trump Mulling Capital Gains Tax Relief as Midterm Sweetener
bullets.body: The Trump administration is reportedly considering capital gains tax cuts ahead of midterm elections as a market sentiment boost and voter incentive. No specific legislative timeline was disclosed, but the signal is potentially meaningful for equity positioning.
